Who it’s forAnyone who needs to feel ORA before they work on it. A new instructor on her first day. A photographer before a shoot. A writer before a caption. Angela, when she needs to remember why she started.
01 The name what ORA means ЧАС +
0 / 00
ŌRA (Latin, n.) /ˈoː.ra/ hour; a measured passage of time.
ЧАС (Macedonian, n.) /t͡ʃas/ hour; class; lesson. A single word carrying two meanings at once.

“ОВА Е ТВОЈ ЧАС“ in Macedonian, can be read in two ways:

This is your hour. This is your class. Both are true. Every other studio in Skopje sells access; to a machine, a class, or a floor. ORA holds space for an hour that belongs entirely to you: sixty uninterrupted minutes designed to restore, strengthen, and reconnect. The hour is the canvas. Everything else exists to shape what unfolds within it.

02 Where it came from the founder’s story TWO YEARS +

Angela was twenty-two when leukemia put her in a hospital bed for two years. She came home at forty-five kilograms. The way back was built one movement at a time, and each discipline gave back a different part of her. None could have done the others’ work. That is the whole argument for five disciplines under one roof. The story came first and the product came out of it, in that order.

01strengthFirst, because she had to be able to carry herself.
02pilatesThen, when her body asked for something quieter.
03cyclingThen, when she needed to feel alive rather than merely upright.

Before ORA there was HUMN, the first Macedonian activewear brand made for women, which Angela co-founded. ORA opens to a community she has already built.

03 The Room space, material, light, hospitality Standard 150 M² +
Ninety-five minutes in the building for a sixty-minute class · one square is five minutes

150 m² arranged so it behaves like four hundred

One Movement Room. One Atrium. What happens between them is the part nobody else in Skopje is building. The Atrium is open to the sky, with a living tree and an oak bench. She arrives fifteen minutes early on purpose and opens her laptop. She leaves twenty minutes late because she is talking to the woman she rode beside. Music from the class carries through, and that is deliberate: the Atrium is the studio’s living room. This is Skopje’s café ritual brought inside the brand, since coffee is already the reason people here arrive early and stay late. ORA takes that habit and puts a movement room beside it.

The room is the argument. Everything else is commentary.
What the room holds toHow it reads on a given day
LightNatural light leads, and never lands on her body.
SoundMusic is chosen for the hour rather than left running.
MaterialNothing artificial pretends to be alive. No motivational posters. No overbranding.
CleanlinessClean is the standard, held every day rather than the day before an inspection.
AirFaintly of cedar, with no commercial cleaner and no incense.
04 The Movement five doors, one practice Integration FIVE HOURS +
A healthy body is not built by one discipline.
01strengthBarbell and bodyweight, heavy work, controlled reps. Low light. RnB and hip hop, loud enough to disappear into. The day she lifts what matters.
02runningTreadmill intervals, pace and breath. The day she moves fast and does not stop.
03cyclingLights down, sound up, forty-five minutes of rhythm. Latin, RnB, hip hop. Angela on the front bike, singing. Healthy clubbing, which is her own phrase for it.
04pilatesBreath, core, control. Afro house underneath, quiet. The body learns to listen.
05yogaNear silence. Room tone. She comes back to presence, then goes home.

Her body picks the one it needs today

Five doors into one practice. Every hour has its own sound. Playlists and choreography are made in-house and changed monthly, so the room never becomes a rerun. The instructor knows her name before she sits down, in every class and every discipline.

05 The Woman who she is, what she leaves with Return SIXTY MINUTES +

Everything at ORA exists for one purpose: her. The room welcomes her. The movement challenges her. But neither is the destination. They are simply the path back to herself. She arrives carrying deadlines, expectations, responsibilities and noise. For one hour, all of it stays outside. What remains is the woman beneath it all. She doesn’t leave as someone new. She leaves as more of herself.

She does not come to be fixed. She comes to come back.
06 Community different reasons, the same hour ONE PLACE +

ORA was born around the belief that every woman needs time for herself, but that every woman will use that time differently. Some come for strength. Others for confidence, balance, energy, or peace. Different reasons, different stories, different lives; All coming together in the same place, for the same hour: one that belongs entirely to them.

She does not come to be fixed. She comes back to herself.

ORA / BRAND STORY
What this isHow ORA speaks and behaves. Personality, tone, the words we use and refuse, how things get named, which language goes where, how credits are explained, approved copy, and what the team says and does at the door.
Who it’s forEveryone who speaks or acts as ORA. The receptionist, the instructors, whoever runs Instagram, any copywriter or translator. If you are about to write a caption, answer a message, or greet a woman at the door, the answer is in here.
Section 1 · Personality
1.1 Who ORA is the person behind the voice SPRING +
Age
Around thirty.
Speech
Speaks with intention: nothing unnecessary, every word heard.
Style
Her own, unmistakable.
Register
Serious most of the time, sharp when she is not.
Around her
You feel safe, appreciated, free to ask anything.

Would she say this?

ORA is written as a person rather than as a set of adjectives, because a person is something you can check a sentence against. Whoever is holding the phone, the pen or the microphone asks the one question above, and the answer is usually obvious inside a second.

She’s not the sun. She’s not the cloud. She’s spring.
1.2 How ORA speaks six rules SAY IT, THEN STOP +
  1. Say the thing, then stop. The instinct to add one more line of reassurance is the instinct to sound like everyone else.
  2. Describe the fact, not the feeling. “The lights go down and the music comes up” does more work than “an unforgettable experience”. She can feel things without being told to.
  3. Address her directly. You more often than we. ORA talks to one woman, never to an audience.
  4. No exclamation marks. Certainty does not need them.
  5. Never sell inside the hour. Selling happens before she arrives and at reception. Once she is in the room, nothing is being sold to her.
  6. Say women, not girls, in anything written. Spoken, in the room, warmth is the team’s own. Written, it is women.

The same voice on a sign, on Instagram and at the door

Short sentences, plain words. Warm, never cute. Certain, never loud. The six rules above are the whole of it, and they hold in Macedonian as well as in English, since none of them is about vocabulary. A caption, a signage plate, a reply to a message and a sentence said at reception all come out of the same mouth.

1.3 The words ours and never ours TWO LISTS +
The lexicon · both lists set the same size, so only the wording separates them
Ours
Your hour · room · return · movement · community · rhythm · method · honest · real · earned · felt · built · here · now · hers · ours · healthy clubbing · coming back to yourself.
Never ours
“Ready to crush your goals.” “Transform your body.” “Snap back.” “Beast mode.” “Bikini season.” Emoji-stacked captions. Countdown urgency.

Anything that turns her body into a project she is failing

Every phrase on the right shouts at her, and most of them tell her the body she walked in with is the thing to be fixed. Countdown urgency and emoji stacks belong to the same instinct: they treat her attention as something to be taken rather than earned. The left-hand list is eighteen words long and stays that way, since a voice is a set of words used often enough to become recognisable.

The mark

Pick the language for the sentence and finish it there

Ова е твој час is the one line that only works in Macedonian, and translating it destroys the double meaning. The mark is a placed file in every language. Everything English on the list is a word she already recognises from the studios she follows, which is the test: if she has to learn a word to use the timetable, the timetable is wrong. The two are never mixed inside a single sentence.

2.3 Explaining credits a language problem Revenue TWELVE CLASSES +
The same offer, twice · the second one sells
Wrong
Buy a 12-credit package and redeem across disciplines.
Right
Twelve classes. Use them on anything. Cycling one day, yoga the next.

Never lead with the word credits

Most women in Skopje have only ever bought a flat monthly gym fee. Credits are unfamiliar, and unfamiliar costs money at the point of sale. The fix is language, not a discount, so lead with classes. If she asks a second question, the answer is always the same shape: she is buying classes, not access, and no discipline is locked behind a different payment.

One membership. Any of the five. You choose on the day.

Section 3 · At the door
3.1 Before she arrives the schedule FIFTEEN NAMES +
The schedule is not a list. It is fifteen women’s names, each with a small story we already know.

The brand is audited here more than anywhere else

This section is Angela’s own protocol, held as written. The team already knows she is coming. The booking system gives reception every name on the day’s schedule by the hour, and the front desk reads the names at the start of the shift. They know who has been here before. They know who is new.

3.2 The first three seconds room, silence, person IN THAT ORDER +
01The roomLight from the Atrium falls into the entrance. The concrete is warm. No fluorescent strip. The air smells faintly of cedar, with no commercial cleaner and no incense.
02The silenceNot the silence of an empty space, the silence of a considered one. Music is playing below the threshold of being noticed.
03The woman at receptionNot behind a counter that hides her. Not on her phone. She is reading, or making a note, or arranging the tray of Member Cards.

The first thing she notices is the room

The order is the point. Reception comes third, after the light and the quiet have already done their work. The moment the door opens, whatever the woman at the desk was doing turns into attention on whoever has walked in.

This is the first message of the brand. The room was waiting for you. The person was here, present, before you arrived.
3.3 The greeting word for word FIRST TIME +
First time, word for word

Hi. You found us. Are you Marija?

Welcome, I’m Pavlina. Come in. Let me show you around before we start.

Her name, then the team’s name, then the room

Two lines, and each does one job. The first says she was expected. The second gives her a name to use back, and moves straight into the walkthrough so she never has to stand and decide what happens next.

3.4 The walkthrough sixty seconds WE DO NOT POINT +
In the Atrium

This is the Atrium. You can wait here before class, there’s a smoothie bar if you want something. After class this is where most of the women stay for fifteen, twenty minutes. Some bring their laptops in the mornings. The light is good here all day.

At the Movement Room glass

That’s the Movement Room. All five disciplines happen in there: strength, running, cycling, pilates, yoga. Each one has its own time. Today is cycling. The bikes are set up.

At the changing rooms

Changing rooms are down the hall. Lockers on the left. Showers on the right. Towels are ready for you.

Sixty seconds, ninety if she is slow

We walk her through, and we do not point. The walkthrough does three things at once. It gives her geographical certainty, so she never has to ask. It shows her everything has been thought of before she needed it. And it establishes the Atrium and the Movement Room as two different places with two different jobs, before she has used either.

3.5 In the room the instructor HER NAME +
The instructor knows her name before she sits down. Every class, every discipline.

Greet the woman next to you

The instructor greets the women already there, asks how the last class went, and introduces the new woman by name. During class she goes to each woman individually for position and posture. After a well-executed series she uses the phrase greet the woman next to you, which is how strangers in a dark room become a community without anyone announcing it.

3.6 Leaving the smoothie, the question SAME TIME TOMORROW +
At the door, reception looks up after her

Are you joining us same time tomorrow?

Her smoothie is already being made

She ordered before class and reception remembered. Reception remembers what she has, and remembers when she changes her mind. The question at the door is the last thing she hears, and it assumes she is coming back.

Section 4 · The line
4.1 What ORA refuses five refusals FIVE +
  1. Nothing we would not put in our own bodies.
  2. No colour, material or finish that does not belong to the brand. Not for a sponsor, not for a season.
  3. No one who treats this as a job. Skill can be trained. Arrogance cannot be removed.
  4. We do not compete on price. If price is the objection, the answer is the room.
  5. We do not become mass. The finite funnel is a constraint we accept, not a problem we widen our way out of.

Every one of these costs money to keep

That is what makes them refusals rather than preferences. The sponsor with a budget, the talented instructor with a temper and the quiet week in July are the tests, and they arrive in the first year. The answer to all three is written above, so that nobody has to invent one under pressure.

ORA / BRAND CHARACTER
What this isHow ORA looks. The visual system logic, the logo, grid, type, color and art direction.
Who it's forAnyone making something physical or digital in ORA's name. The signage fabricator, the printer, the web developer, the photographer, any designer who touches this after Denica.
01VISUAL SYSTEM LOGIC+

One hour. Sixty minutes. A measure of time that becomes the foundation of the visual system.

We translate the structure of an hour into a visual language, using its divisions, rhythm and proportions as the basis of the system. The grid here is adopted rather than designed: it already exists inside the hour. We measure in minutes rather than millimetres. Every distance on every surface is a duration: a margin is one minute, a text column is a quarter of an hour, an image runs half past. Change the format and the millimetres change, but the minutes never do. This is what allows a poster, a screen and a wall to remain the same object. The grid is the hour laid flat, and every surface is a sixty-minute class drawn at a different size. The field is sixty squares across and one square is one minute. The margin is one square, regardless of the surface. The squares group into columns the way the face groups minutes: twelve columns of five, or six of ten. The square itself grows with the surface, drawn in pixels on screen and points in print. What never changes is that there are sixty of them. Time is the only material here. The hour is a structure ORA builds in, and every surface is that structure at a different size.

02LOGODownloads+
Construction60 × 60 minutes
Hour → clock holds the hour → clock becomes ORA’s mark

The visual system begins with the measure of an hour.

The logo gives that measure a physical form: the clock, a structure designed to hold it. In the same way, ORA exists to hold an hour entirely for her, creating the space for that time to belong to her. ORA adopts this structure as its mark, turning the idea of holding time into a visual symbol.

Logo variations

The ClockThe symbolic expression

The Clock is the distilled symbol of ORA and the most direct visual expression of its central idea. It can be used independently as a recognisable brand mark, or paired with the slogan to create a more conceptual expression of the brand. Its simplicity allows it to live across both small and large scale applications, from digital touchpoints to the physical environment.

SVG PNG PDF
The FrameThe structural expression

The Frame extends the ORA mark into a graphic structure. It can become part of the composition itself: framing, containing and organising imagery, typography or information. It allows the identity to move beyond identification and become an active element of the wider visual system.

SVG PNG PDF
The SignatureThe primary expression

The Signature is the primary expression of ORA and the form used most consistently across the brand. It brings together the ORA name and its visual mark into a complete brand signature, creating the clearest expression of the identity. It can stand independently or be paired with the slogan when the brand idea needs to be expressed alongside the mark.

SVG PNG PDF
The WordmarkThe written expression

The Wordmark is the name of ORA in its simplest typographic form. It is used when the brand is being written about, referenced or identified within communication, from editorial and press to partnerships, listings and other contexts where the name appears as part of a text. It can be expressed in Latin as ORA and in Cyrillic as ора, so the identity adapts to the language and the context it appears in.

03TYPEDownloads+
The voiceHelvetica Neue
Helvetica Neue ZIP

The Cyrillic cut is a separate licence and is not in this file.

The dataPT Mono
PT Mono TTF OFL licence

Helvetica Neue is the voice. PT Mono is the data.

Every surface in the system is some ratio of the two, and the ratio is the tone. A manifesto is nearly all voice. A timetable is nearly all data. Each face is shown above at the sizes it is allowed, one square apart. The voice has three: the hour at 40, the half at 20, the quarter at 10, named for the depth of line each one occupies. The data has two, because it is barred from display and starts at the half. Below its floor sits 5, drawn dashed because its line runs at 7.5 and lands under the quarter, which is why it belongs to timestamps and credits and never to anything setting the rhythm of a page.

Helvetica also carries the disciplines.

Weight becomes a measure of effort: Strength demands the most and is set in the heaviest weight; Yoga demands the least and is set in the lightest. As the effort decreases, the type becomes lighter and more open. Colour completes the distinction. There are no separate logos: the disciplines are identified entirely through typography and colour.

strength

Strength carries the most, so it is set in Black at minus two percent. The heaviest weight needs the tightest tracking to hold together: maximum load, minimum air.

Black · −2%
running

Running drops to Bold and the tracking opens one step to minus one percent. Weight is coming off the body and the letters loosen with it, the way a stride settles once it finds its rhythm.

Bold · −1%
cycling

Cycling sits at Medium and zero, the middle of the ramp. Nothing is being lifted and nothing needs correcting: natural weight, natural width.

Medium · 0
pilates

Pilates settles to Regular and opens to plus four percent. The weight is light enough now that the letters need space between them to keep their shape.

Regular · +4%
yoga

Yoga is Light at plus twelve percent, the lightest weight and the widest tracking. Without that air the line would collapse into grey. With it, the letters breathe apart until they are almost no longer a word, which is where the hour ends.

Light · +12%

The slash in data

The slash in PT Mono should not be confused with the diagonal of the mark. The slash is a typographic character used to present data, information, and measurements. The diagonal is the clock hand, used within the mark and as a graphic element derived from it. They are not interchangeable: the slash belongs to typography and data, while the diagonal belongs to the visual identity.

The brand, three sides, five disciplines. Eight colours.

Oxblood runs the full width at the top because it is the brand itself and answers to neither tier. Under it sit the three sides, and under those the five disciplines. Concrete is the Room, ORA Red is the Movement, Blood Red is the Woman. Near-Black is strength, Charcoal is running, ORA Red is cycling, Steel is pilates, White is yoga. ORA Red is the one colour that appears twice, and the two uses run opposite ways: the Movement takes red as ink on white, cycling takes white on red.

One gradient. Nothing is ever set on it.

ORA Red to Blood Red, the Movement handing off to the Woman, and it is the only gradient the system has. It is a ground and governs everything atmospheric. Blur, glow, grain and gradient sit behind and around, never on the words. Type stays sharp at every size and the drawn hand never blurs.

05ART DIRECTIONDownloads+

ONE SYSTEM, FIVE EXPRESSIONS

ORA's art direction starts with one shared visual system: the red, the two faces, typography and the field. The five disciplines are not given separate identities. Instead, the same elements are used in different ways: changing in scale, placement, weight and intensity. This makes each discipline feel distinct while keeping everything clearly part of ORA.

strengthcontrolled / grounded
runningpropulsive / repetitive
cyclingcyclical / repetitive
pilatesprecise / controlled
yogaheld / fluid

TYPE CREATES THE RHYTHM

Type gives each discipline its own sense of movement. Weight represents physical load, moving from Black for Strength to Light for Yoga, while tracking opens as the intensity decreases. PT Mono is used as data: a label paired with its value, and placed directly into the field rather than kept in a fixed information block. Its position changes with the movement of each discipline: Strength clusters and holds, Running moves across the field, Cycling gathers around a centre, Pilates follows precise lines, and Yoga uses only two points and leaves the rest open. Type makes the character of each movement visible without literally illustrating it.

strengthheld, clustered, not travelling
runningstepping forward, one direction
cyclingaround a centre, returning
pilatesexact, few, on the lines
yogastill, wide apart, mostly air

COLOUR SHOWS THE MOVEMENT

Red shows the continuity of movement rather than physical effort. Its amount changes from discipline to discipline. Strength has no red in the image because its movement is controlled and contained. Running introduces red as a trace through the image. Cycling uses more red, allowing it to become the main field. Pilates reduces it to a small accent, while Yoga removes it from the image completely and keeps it only in the type. Colour helps the viewer feel how each discipline moves: from contained, to continuous, and back to stillness.
